title: Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-08-10
body:
Infrastructure Weekly Update - 2026-08-10
Owner: Anika Shah
Contributors: Miguel Torres, Priya Nair, Ethan Cole

High-level summary:
- Overall GPU fleet health is stable. Average utilization across serving pools was 68% for the week (up 4pp week-over-week) driven by increased traffic from a couple of hosted customers and early testing traffic for PHX-APAC pilot.
- We saw one minor regional incident in us-west2 on 2026-08-09 impacting dedicated cluster provisioning (approx 43 minutes). Root cause: autoscaler regression in the provisioning path after a recent kubelet upgrade; rollback and hotfix applied. No customer data exposed.
- Capacity planning: Q4 demand forecasting shows a potential need for an additional ~640 A100-equivalent GPUs cluster capacity to meet committed Dedicated SLAs and expected hosted growth. Early procurement conversations started.

Metrics & capacity snapshot (week of 2026-08-03 -> 2026-08-09):
- Total GPUs available (prod serving): 6,720 (mixed A100/H100 pools)
- Avg cluster utilization (prod serving): 68%
- Peak per-region utilization:
  - us-west2: 86% peak (evening spike 02:00-03:00 UTC)
  - us-east1: 62%
  - eu-west1: 57%
  - ap-southeast1 (pilot): 31% (still warm-up)
- Pending reservation requests: 2 (enterprise customers) totaling 256 GPUs to be provisioned in Dedicated pools by 2026-09-15.
- Autoscaler scale-up latency (median): 45s; worst-case observed during incident: ~6m

Incidents & postmortem notes:
- Incident: us-west2 provisioning regression (2026-08-09, 01:12-01:55 UTC)
  - Impact: Failed new node joins causing Dedicated provisioning to fail for ~43m; existing serving traffic degraded but autoscaling of alternative pools mitigated major customer impact.
  - Root cause: kubelet config change introduced in patch (kube-1.29.2) incompatible with our node-init hook.
  - Mitigation: rolled back node image to kube-1.28.x and hotfixed node-init script; full test plan added to PR gating.
  - Action items:
    1) Add kubelet smoke test to image pipeline (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-08-17)
    2) Add cross-region provisioning e2e to nightly CI (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2026-08-24)
    3) Update runbook with rollback steps and postmortem link (owner: Anika Shah, due: 2026-08-13)

Operational changes this week:
- We enabled per-route priority routing for two high-value customers in us-west2 to reduce tail latency during spikes (config change applied 2026-08-07). Observed 12% P99 latency improvement for those routes during peak windows.
- Started phased kernel upgrade in eu-west1 (canary group) with updated NVIDIA driver 535. Results so far: no regressions in inference latency; one outlier pod required node reboot. Canary to continue next week.
- Launched PHX-APAC pilot: a small warm pool in ap-southeast1 (8 H100s) to validate latency for APAC early customers. Initial perf: 20-30ms improvement median RTT for APAC test traffic.

Capacity planning & procurement:
- Forecasting models updated with July usage shape and Q3 pipeline. Two scenarios for Q4:
  - Base: +320 GPUs required to maintain <75% avg utilization across serving pools.
  - Upside: +640 GPUs needed should two large Dedicated bookings finalize in Q3.
- Procurement: finance & procurement engaged; target to secure spot/reserved mix by end of August. Expected lead time for certain SKUs (H100) is 8-12 weeks; A100 equivalent availability is better (3-6 weeks).
- Short-term mitigations being put in place:
  - Increase cross-region fallback capacity for top 10 customers (config & policy change, owner: Ethan Cole, due: 2026-08-21)
  - Enable more aggressive prefix KV caching for non-latency-sensitive routes to reduce load (owner: Peiyun / Serving Runtime, coordination ticket: JIRA-ENG-7105)

Standup notes / running log (high level):
- 2026-08-04
  - Node pool health: minor pod evictions in eu-west1 during kernel canary; observed due to out-of-date autoscaler thresholds.
  - Action: adjust eviction thresholds and re-run soak tests.
- 2026-08-05
  - Capacity planning sync with Product: Product asked for contingency plan if Dedicated commit exceeds forecasts; outlined options (burst to hosted, preemptible mix, reserved procurement).
- 2026-08-06
  - PHX-APAC pilot traffic validation completed; observed cold-starts for some models due to missing quantized artifacts in region cache. Action: pre-warm and replicate quant artifacts (owner: Miguel Torres).
- 2026-08-07
  - Per-route priority routing enabled for two customers; metric checks scheduled for 48h.
- 2026-08-09
  - Incident during provisioning (see incident section). After rollback, provisioning passed tests.

Open requests / asks from other teams:
- Model-serving: needs an extra 128 GPUs in us-west2 for a week of heavy evals (2026-08-24 -> 2026-08-30). Request ticket: JIRA-MODEL-998. Proposal: schedule temporary burst capacity using reserved on-demand pool; ask infra to approve config (owner: Anika Shah to coordinate with Product and Sales).
- Solutions Eng: wants APAC pilot extended to 24 H100s for customer POC (requested start 2026-09-01). Need procurement confirmation and cost estimate (owner: Priya Nair to draft cost note by 2026-08-14).

Risks & concerns:
- SKU lead times for H100 remain a gating factor for Q4 commitments. If procurement delays continue, we'll need to increase cross-region fallbacks and tighten routing policies to preserve SLAs.
- Autoscaler regressions: The recent incident underscores the need for stronger gating for node-image changes and better synthetic e2e tests.

Decisions made:
- Move forward with procurement approval process for up to 640 GPUs (A100/H100 mix) contingent on contract signings in Q3. Procurement kickoff scheduled 2026-08-12.
- Add kubelet smoke tests to image pipeline before any further kube upgrades to production clusters.

Action items (summary):
- Priya Nair: Add kubelet smoke test to image pipeline and own rollout (due 2026-08-17).
- Miguel Torres: Add cross-region provisioning e2e to nightly CI and replicate quant artifacts for APAC (due 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-12 respectively).
- Ethan Cole: Implement cross-region fallback config for top 10 customers (due 2026-08-21).
- Anika Shah: Update runbook with rollback steps and coordinate temporary GPU burst for model-serving evals (due 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-12).
- Priya Nair: Draft cost estimate for APAC pilot scale (due 2026-08-14).

Meeting notes (Capacity sync, 2026-08-09):
Attendees: Anika, Priya, Miguel, Ethan, Sarah (Product), James (Sales)
Key points:
- Discussed Q4 demand scenarios and procurement timelines.
- Sales to prioritize timeline for two large Dedicated deals; decision point by 2026-08-20 to lock procurement quantity.
- Product proposed temporary burst strategy using a mix of spot and reserved capacity; Finance flagged budget needs.

Useful links / references:
- GPU Fleet Runbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/GPU+Fleet+Runbook
- Incident ticket: JIRA-OPS-4821
- Capacity forecast workbook: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c_example
- APAC pilot tracking doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/APAC+Pilot

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding monthly capacity buffer metric in Console so PMs and Sales can see headroom per-region without pinging infra.
- Follow up with Solutions Eng on exact POC customer list for APAC pilot (we should prioritize customers that will actually test during Sept timeframe).

End of update.
